questions.scenario: Summer peak time and the power goes out (light chali gayi)! What is your immediate reaction?

options.text: Grab a torch, check the MCB (fuse box) in the hallway, and check the inverter battery water levels.
Quickly mentally calculate the current load to figure out how many hours the inverter battery will last.
Get annoyed because your aesthetic LED room lighting turned off, and start sketching ideas for battery-powered smart lights.
Take charge, tell everyone to gather in one room to save the inverter battery and keep the remaining AC cooling trapped.

questions.scenario: It's Diwali and half the fairy lights (laris) are tangled and not working. You...

options.text: Sit down with a tester pen, hunt down the broken bulb, cut the wire, and twist it back to complete the circuit.
Wonder how much total electricity the entire society is consuming tonight and the load on the local transformer.
Leave the broken ones aside and focus on arranging the working ones in the most visually stunning pattern on the balcony.
Tell your parents it's a waste of time fixing them, head to the local bazaar, and negotiate a bulk deal for better quality LED laris.

questions.scenario: Your family is buying a brand new AC or fridge. What do you care about the most?

options.text: Looking at the heavy compressor unit and asking the installation bhaiya exactly how the copper wiring will be routed.
Comparing the 3-star vs. 5-star BEE energy rating to calculate the exact electricity bill savings per year.
The sleek design, color, and whether it has a cool Wi-Fi app so you can control it from your phone.
Convincing your parents on which brand offers the best warranty, after-sales service, and overall value for money.

questions.scenario: For your 10th standard Physics project (Electricity chapter), what are you making?

options.text: A fully functional mini water pump or motor using thick copper wire, magnets, and a heavy 9V battery.
A detailed chart explaining how home solar panels can reduce your city's reliance on coal power plants.
A cool mini smart-city model with automated street lights that turn on in the dark using an LDR sensor.
You are the group leader who goes to the electronics market to buy components, divides tasks, and presents the project to the teacher.

questions.scenario: A loose plug socket is sparking in your room. What’s your move?

options.text: Turn off the main switch, grab a screwdriver, open the board, and tighten the loose wire yourself.
Research online to see if the sparking is due to a voltage fluctuation or loose contact, and suggest buying a voltage stabilizer.
Ask your parents to replace the whole dusty switchboard with those fancy modern modular switches with built-in USB ports.
Call the local electrician, negotiate his visiting charge beforehand, and supervise him to make sure he fixes it properly.

questions.scenario: Your society is organizing a huge Ganesh Chaturthi or Durga Puja pandal. How are you helping?

options.text: Helping the sound and light guys run the heavy cables, set up the big speakers, and fix loose connections.
Doing the math to ensure the rented diesel generator is big enough to handle the DJ, halogen lights, and fans without tripping.
Obsessing over programming the decorative LED light sequences so they perfectly sync with the aarti or music.
Managing the budget for the electrical setup, collecting chanda (funds), and bargaining with the tent contractors.

questions.scenario: When you look up at the crazy maze of wires on an Indian street pole, what goes through your mind?

options.text: You try to visually trace which thick black cable is the main power line and which ones are just messy internet/cable wires.
You think about how much electricity is lost in transmission and how moving to underground wiring would save energy.
You think it looks incredibly ugly and imagine how clean and futuristic the street would look if everything was wireless.
You wonder which government department pays the bill for the streetlights and how the municipal corporation manages the cost.

questions.scenario: You finally get a brand new smartphone. What is the first thing that fascinates you?

options.text: The heavy fast-charging brick—you check its wattage and marvel at how the Type-C cable handles that much current without heating.
Diving into the battery settings to analyze which apps are draining the mAh and optimizing background usage for maximum battery life.
Customizing the home screen and immediately connecting it to your Bluetooth speakers or smart bulb app.
Calculating the resale value of your old phone and figuring out if you got the best exchange offer possible.

questions.scenario: You are traveling on a fast train like the Vande Bharat or Shatabdi. What catches your attention?

options.text: Staring out the window at the heavy overhead electric lines and the pantograph connecting them to the train.
Thinking about the massive amount of energy required to accelerate the train and how regenerative braking works.
Appreciating the automatic sliding doors, the sleek reading lights, and the tech-integrated interior design.
Thinking about how much ticket revenue this specific route generates and the logistics of running the train on time.

questions.scenario: Your laptop suddenly shuts down and refuses to turn on. What is your action plan?

options.text: Confidently open the back panel with a tiny screwdriver, disconnect the battery, drain static charge, and plug it back in.
Run a logical diagnostic in your head: Is the charger brick hot? Is the wall socket dead? Let's isolate the variables.
Get annoyed because you were designing something creative, but quickly switch to your tablet to finish the design seamlessly.
Find the warranty card immediately, locate the nearest authorized service center, and plan how to get it fixed without getting scammed.

Field_Electrical_Engineer.title: The Hands-On Fixer (Field Electrical Engineer)
Field_Electrical_Engineer.primary_match_text: You love getting your hands dirty! You are practical, fearless, and always curious about how things work on the inside. You don't just read manuals; you open things up.
Field_Electrical_Engineer.day_in_the_life: Wearing safety gear, heading to massive electrical substations, troubleshooting heavy machinery, and leading a team of technicians to fix live grids on the ground.
Field_Electrical_Engineer.alternative_match_text: If not this, you might really enjoy Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, or Robotics.
Field_Electrical_Engineer.educational_roadmap: 11th-12th: Science (PCM is mandatory). Entrance: Crack JEE Main, Advanced, or State CETs. Degree: B.Tech in Electrical Engineering. Next Steps: Target core engineering jobs in PSUs (like BHEL, NTPC) or giants like L&T.

Power_Systems_Analyst.title: The Grid Optimizer (Power Systems / Renewable Energy Analyst)
Power_Systems_Analyst.primary_match_text: You are a deeply analytical thinker. You see the big picture, love efficiency, and want to solve the country's energy problems using pure logic, math, and data.
Power_Systems_Analyst.day_in_the_life: Sitting in a high-tech control room or research lab, analyzing state-wide power grids on software, designing massive solar farms, and preventing blackouts.
Power_Systems_Analyst.alternative_match_text: You might also excel as a Data Scientist, an Environmental Engineer, or a Research Scientist.
Power_Systems_Analyst.educational_roadmap: 11th-12th: Science (PCM is mandatory). Entrance: Crack JEE Main & Advanced. Degree: B.Tech in Electrical or Energy Engineering. Next Steps: Highly recommended to pursue a Master's (M.Tech/MS) in Renewable Energy or Power Systems.

Smart_Home_Designer.title: The Tech-Aesthete (Smart Home / Electronics Designer)
Smart_Home_Designer.primary_match_text: You sit right at the intersection of technology and creativity. You don't just want things to function; you want them to be smart, sleek, and visually stunning.
Smart_Home_Designer.day_in_the_life: Prototyping cool smart home gadgets, designing sleek PCBs, coding home automation systems, and making everyday appliances 'smart' and beautiful.
Smart_Home_Designer.alternative_match_text: You would also rock in Product Design, UI/UX Design, or Electronics and Communication Engineering (ECE).
Smart_Home_Designer.educational_roadmap: 11th-12th: Science (PCM). Entrance: Crack JEE or CET. Degree: B.Tech in Electronics & Communication (ECE) or Electrical Engineering. Next Steps: Take specialized courses in IoT (Internet of Things) and Embedded Systems.

Energy_Consultant.title: The Power Boss (Energy Consultant / Plant Head)
Energy_Consultant.primary_match_text: You are a natural leader with a sharp business mindset. You understand the tech, but you prefer managing the people, the money, and the grand strategy.
Energy_Consultant.day_in_the_life: Meeting with corporate clients, managing multi-crore budgets for new power projects, leading large teams, and making sure power plants run profitably.
Energy_Consultant.alternative_match_text: Consider pursuing an MBA later to become a top-tier Management Consultant, Investment Banker, or Entrepreneur.
Energy_Consultant.educational_roadmap: 11th-12th: Science (PCM). Degree: B.Tech in Electrical Engineering. Next Steps: Work for 2-3 years, then crack CAT/GMAT to pursue an MBA in Power Management, Operations, or Business Strategy.
